world.description: With the U.S. now leading the Geneva Consensus Declaration, the anti-abortion and anti-LGBTQ+ initiative is seeking to expand its reach across Latin America. Argentina’s decision to join gives the coalition 4 members in the region, while documents obtained by GPAHE show Bolivia recently declined an invitation. Meanwhile, U.S. officials have already begun outreach to Chile, signaling a push to build support for the GCD across the hemisphere.

science.title: Temperature-tunable micropillars enable programmable sorting of particles and cells
science.description: A programmable microfluidic device developed at the Institute of Science Tokyo, Japan, combines deterministic lateral displacement, a microfluidic technique used to separate particles according to size, with temperature-responsive polymer micropillars to dynamically change separation conditions along a single channel. Using this device, researchers successfully separated multiple particle populations. Additionally, they efficiently isolated viable cancer cells, white blood cells and red blood cells from diluted whole blood.

science.title: A bird's eye view of illegal logging and its consequences in the Peruvian Amazon
science.description: When I first arrived in Peru's Allpahuayo-Mishana National Reserve in 2005, a local youth surprised me with an offer to sell me a live owl, despite the fact that we were in a protected area where commercial hunting was prohibited. We set the owl free together, but this turned out to be an early lesson about the vulnerability of tropical protected areas to exploitation, even when laws and policies had been put in place to protect them. At that time, Allpahuayo-Mishana was a newly designated protected area with no paid staff except for its director, who was stationed in the nearby city of Iquitos.
